chapter: European recordings and return to America
title: Conducting with Stockhausen for Danish radio
summary: His sextet played at the Tivoli between two orchestras performing Stockhausen, and he became friends with the composer.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did a concert with a very modern composer – the modern composer at the time. I shouldn’t start this at this time in the morning.
Yeah, German. What’s his name? Stockhausen.
Yeah. We did a – for Danish radio they hired my sextet to be part of two symphony orchestras at once. There must have been 150 musicians on stage doing
Stockhausen’s latest work, and in the intermission featuring George Russell’s sextet. It was really out there.
That was done at the Tivoli in Denmark.
At the Tivoli in Denmark, okay, for Danish national radio.
Yeah. What’s the big town in Denmark, the biggest?
This finds us pretty much at the beginning of the ’70s, and to set the stage a little bit . . .
Incidentally, Stockenhausen and I became pretty good friends.
How did you find him? Tell us a little bit about him, I mean, just in terms of any remembrance that you may have.
I had – I knew a few girls. Stockhausen loves women. So I introduced him to this one luscious lady. From then on, he took off. Europe was very exciting, my experience in Europe.
